# Set-up

This markdown performs doublet calling using scDblFinder on the whole, uncorrected Ovarian Cancer 10x Flex dataset. This includes:

- removal of low quality cells - note, no mito filter

- scDblFinder doublet calling, split per sample

- export of results as `qs2` object, as well as in 10X cellranger output format


## Load libraries

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(here)
  library(glue)
  library(DropletUtils)
  library(scran)
  library(scater)
  library(scuttle)
  library(scales)
  library(readr)
  library(Seurat)
  library(scDblFinder)
  library(scMerge)
  library(ggpubr)
  library(BiocParallel)
  library(clustree)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(scMerge)
  library(Matrix)
  library(SeuratDisk)
  library(qs2)
  library(patchwork)
})


```

## Load data

The cellranger outputs were downloaded from the [10X website](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/20k-mixture-of-nsclc-dtcs-from-7-donors-3-v3-1-with-intronic-reads-3-1-standard).


```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

counts <- Read10X_h5(here('data/OvarianCancer_10xFlex/17k_Ovarian_Cancer_scFFPE_count_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5'))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = c("counts" = counts))
sce

```

Add sample names based on 10X Flex barcode structure. 

```{r}
sce$Barcode <- colnames(sce)
sce$Sample <- substring(sce$Barcode, first = 18, last = 26)
```



# QC filtering 

Low quality cells will be removed prior to performing doublet detection. Our main goal here is to eliminate cells with a very low library size and/or number of genes detected, as their presence may interfere with doublet calling. 10X flex does not have any probes for ribosomal genes. For this dataset, we will not use a % mitochondrial threshold as 10X reports a specific cancer cell subtype that has particularly high proportions of mitochondrial RNA. To avoid loss of biological meaningful cells, we only perform a library size and features detected filter. 

Add per cell summary metrics

```{r}
is.mito <- grepl(pattern = "^MT", rownames(sce))
sce <- addPerCellQCMetrics(sce, subsets = list(mito = is.mito))

new_meta <- sce@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>% #immediately clean up metadata
  dplyr::rename(., nfeatures = detected, ncount = sum) %>%
  select(., -c("subsets_mito_sum", "subsets_mito_detected", "total"))
sce@colData <- new_meta %>% DataFrame()

```

```{r, include=FALSE}
rm(new_meta, is.mito); gc()
```


Plot distribution of library sizes, detected genes and %mito, split for each sample. The dotted lines indicate selected thresholds. 

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
p1 <- plotColData(
    sce,
    "ncount",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 200,
               linetype = "dotted")

p2 <- plotColData(
    sce,
    "nfeatures",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 150,
               linetype = "dotted")
  
p3 <- plotColData(
    sce,
    "subsets_mito_percent",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) 

p1+p2+p3 + plot_layout(ncol=2)
```


Remove cells. 

```{r}
sce$high_quality_cell <- (sce$ncount >= 200) & (sce$nfeatures >= 150) 

sce@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
  group_by(Sample,high_quality_cell) %>% 
  summarise(count = n()) %>% 
  group_by(Sample) %>% 
  mutate(., percent_kept = round(count/sum(count),5)) %>% 
  filter(., high_quality_cell == FALSE) %>% 
  select(Sample, count, percent_kept) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(removed_cell=count) %>% 
  knitr::kable() 

```

```{r}
sce_filtered <- sce[rowSums(counts(sce)) > 50, sce$high_quality_cell == T] #also remove genes that are barely expressed
sce_filtered
```

Plot distribution after QC

```{r, fig.align='center', fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
p1 <- plotColData(
    sce_filtered,
    "ncount",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) 

p2 <- plotColData(
    sce_filtered,
    "nfeatures",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
  
p3 <- plotColData(
    sce_filtered,
    "subsets_mito_percent",
    x = "Sample",
    colour_by = "Sample",
    point_size = 1) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) 

p1+p2+p3 + plot_layout(ncol=2)
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
rm(sce, p1, p2, p3);gc()
```


# Doublet calling - scDblFinder

Running scDblFinder for doublet detection. We have already removed cells with very low library size and very high mitochondrial content. scDblFinder requires a standard workflow to be run on the SCE. As recommended by the authors, we are applying scDblFinder for each sample separately by using the `samples` parameter. 

```{r}
#standard workflow
sce_filtered <- logNormCounts(sce_filtered) %>%
  runPCA() %>%
  runUMAP()

#scDblFinder
set.seed(1997)
sce_filtered <- scDblFinder(sce_filtered,
                   clusters = T,
                   dbr.sd = 1, #removing doublet rate assumption 
                   samples = "Sample", 
                   verbose=F) 
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
gc()
```


# Clean up metadata

Before we export the data, lets tidy up the metadata. 

```{r, echo=FALSE}
new_meta <- sce_filtered@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
  select(., c("Sample", "ncount", "nfeatures", "subsets_mito_percent", "sizeFactor", "scDblFinder.class", "scDblFinder.score"))
sce_filtered@colData <- new_meta %>% DataFrame()

```

```{r, include=FALSE}
rm(new_meta);gc()
```


# Export

## qs2 export

Exporting whole object.

```{r}
filename <- here("output/data/OvarianCancer_10xFlex/OvarianCancer_10xFlex_whole_dataset_processed_scdblfinder.qs2")
qs_save(object = sce_filtered, file = filename)
```

## 10x v3 folder format whole dataset

Using the cellranger output format also saves a lot of space and allows us to load in specific things we need, such as just the metadata, or just barcodes. 

```{r}
DropletUtils::write10xCounts(path = here("output/data/OvarianCancer_10xFlex/OvarianCancer_10xFlex_whole_dataset_processed/"),
                               x = counts(sce_filtered),
                               version = "3")
#export metadata
write_tsv(x=as.data.frame(sce_filtered@colData), file=here("output/data/OvarianCancer_10xFlex/OvarianCancer_10xFlex_whole_dataset_processed/metadata.tsv"))

```
